justice: The street allocates substantial space to motor traffic with multiple wide asphalt lanes, while the pedestrian realm on the right appears comparatively narrow, indicating an uneven distribution of street space among road users.
A separated side path is visible on the right behind a planted verge, which gives non-motorized users some dedicated space rather than forcing them into the carriageway.
Accessibility is only moderate because the visible path looks smooth and level, but no curb ramps, tactile paving, marked crossings, or other barrier-free crossing features are visible in this scene.
safety: Lane markings are clear and the roadway is wide, which helps organize vehicle movement and reduces ambiguity for drivers.
Streetlights are installed continuously along the corridor, supporting visibility and perceived safety after dark.

Safety for all users is limited by the high-speed arterial character: a motorbike is traveling in the carriageway and no clearly protected pedestrian crossing or visibly protected cycling facility is shown.
livability: The corridor feels low in everyday street life because there are no visible shops, active frontages, seating areas, or people gathering along the edge.
Trees and planted medians add greenery and soften the road environment, which improves basic environmental quality.
The overall scene is dominated by long travel lanes and traffic movement, making it function more as a transport corridor than a socially active public street.
sustainability: Continuous rows of trees and planted strips on both sides and in the median contribute to urban greening and potential shade and air-quality benefits.
The broad, smooth side path on the right suggests accommodation for non-motorized travel, which is more sustainable than a car-only street design.

Sustainability is constrained because the visible cross-section still prioritizes a large amount of asphalt roadway for motor vehicles, and no bus lane, bus stop, or obvious stormwater feature is visible.
aesthetics: The avenue has a clean and orderly appearance, with consistent lane markings, uniform streetlights, and maintained planting beds.
Rows of mature trees on the right and smaller trees in the median create a coherent green edge that improves visual quality.
Aesthetics are somewhat reduced by the very wide expanse of asphalt and the sparse architectural frontage, which make the scene feel monotonous despite the landscaping.
comfort: Thermal comfort is mixed: trees provide some shade along the edges, but the main roadway and much of the visible path are exposed to strong sun.
Physical comfort is fairly good because the road surface and side path appear smooth and even, with no visible potholes or clutter obstructing movement.

Psychological comfort is only moderate since the street is very wide and traffic-oriented, which can make walking alongside it feel exposed and less relaxed even though traffic volume appears light at this moment.
walkability: A continuous pedestrian path appears to exist on the right side, separated from the carriageway by a planted verge, which supports basic walking continuity.
Walkability is weakened because the street is very wide and no marked crosswalk, pedestrian refuge, or signalized crossing is visible in the image.
The walking environment lacks visible benches, storefronts, and close human-scale activity, so it may be functional for movement but not especially inviting for pedestrians.
